name: Hydrochlorothiazide
summary: The workhorse thiazide diuretic and first-line antihypertensive; blocks sodium reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule and lowers blood pressure both acutely and chronically.
mechanism: Inhibits the Na+-Cl− cotransporter (NCC) in the distal convoluted tubule, causing natriuresis; with chronic use, peripheral resistance falls, sustaining the antihypertensive effect.

dosing.maxDose: 50 mg/day (higher doses add toxicity, not efficacy)

safety.pregnancy: Not first-line for hypertension in pregnancy (fetal/neonatal risks)
safety.lactation: Excreted in milk (small amounts); may suppress lactation
warnings: Hypokalemia and hyponatremia — the dose-limiting metabolic effects
safety.overdose: Electrolyte depletion and dehydration; replace volume and electrolytes.

indications: Mild to moderate edema in heart failure and hepatic disease
clinicalPearls: The antihypertensive dose-response plateaus at 25 mg — pushing higher doses mainly adds metabolic side effects.
Combines naturally with ACE inhibitors/ARBs, counteracting their hyperkalemia while they blunt its potassium loss.
good: Uncomplicated hypertension, including elderly and Black patients, where thiazides are proven first-line.
bad: Gout, hypokalemia, sulfonamide allergy, or pregnancy.
